reasoning_traces.think:
Grouping loss (GL) measures the average variance of true posteriors within calibrated probability bins, defined as GL = E_S[ Var( P(Y=1|X) | score = s ) ]. It serves as a lower bound on recoverable resolution, indicating whether signal remains after calibration. If GL is large, it suggests that within-bin variation in outcomes persists, implying potential for model improvement. Conversely, if GL ≈ 0, it may indicate either market efficiency (no exploitable signal) or collapse of signal into a single flat number. A permutation null test compares observed GL against a distribution generated by shuffling outcomes within bins, establishing statistical significance. The test determines whether real structure exists (GL > c_0.95) or if the market has already priced in the signal (GL ≤ c_0.95). Feature clustering ensures that GL is computed using relevant variables; without such features, GL degenerates to pure noise (p(1-p) ≈ 0.25). This framework enables GSE to make adaptive decisions about model building and feature expansion.
